songs.title: Wicked Game
songs.role: Clean arpeggio rhythm + lead noodling over the vamp
songs.linkQuality: Songsterr acoustic rhythm track (Acoustic Guitar Left)
songs.scaleHint: B minor / B Dorian. The E major chord carries a G#, so B Dorian (B C# D E F# G# A) is the singing note choice over the vamp; B minor pentatonic is the safe fallback. Open position works too: the same pentatonic sits around the open Bm shapes at frets 0-2.
songs.mustKnow: One 4-bar loop the whole song: Bm (1 bar) A (1 bar) E (2 bars). Arpeggiate, do not strum hard.
songs.fallback: Open Bm barre, open A, open E on repeat. Play fewer notes and let them ring.
songs.rehearsalNotes: Noodling setlist extra. Skip for shows unless called. Slow-burn improv vehicle: ride the Bm A E vamp until faded or cued.

songs.title: Comfortably Numb
songs.role: Clean rhythm + extended lead noodling over the outro vamp
songs.linkQuality: Songsterr rhythm guitar track (Black Strat, Rhythm Guitar)
songs.scaleHint: B minor is home: B minor pentatonic (B D E F# A) covers the Bm A G Em verse cycle and the whole outro solo. The pre-chorus section sits in D major, the relative major, so the same seven notes work over D and A; over the C and G bars drop to C natural (D Mixolydian) or just lean on the D major pentatonic. The outro solo also lives in box 2 at 10th: 10-12 / 9-12 / 9-12 / 9-11 / 10-12 / 10-12.
songs.mustKnow: Verse cycle is 4 bars: Bm, A, G to Em inside one bar, Bm. Pre-chorus cycle is 8 bars: D A D A C G C G. The outro solo rides the verse cycle.
songs.fallback: Open Em, G, C, D and A with a barre Bm at the 2nd fret. If the lead gets away from you, hold the vamp chords and let them ring.

songs.title: White Rabbit
songs.role: Solo arrangement: rhythm chords under your own vocal
songs.linkQuality: Songsterr rhythm guitar track (Rhythm Guitar, Paul Kantner)
songs.scaleHint: Home is F# with a flamenco color. The verse rides F# major up one fret to G major, which is F# Phrygian dominant (F# G A# B C# D E), so aim at the F# and A# chord tones and treat the G as the spice note. Do not use the box over the verse: its A natural fights the F# chord A#. The box is for the A bars, the chorus and the long A outro, where A major pentatonic and F# minor pentatonic are the same five notes. On the half bar of C, sit out or slide the C# down to C. The E to A bridge takes plain E major pentatonic.
songs.pentatonicBox: F# minor box 1 at 2nd for A major: 2-5 / 2-4 / 2-4 / 2-4 / 2-5 / 2-5
songs.mustKnow: One bolero cell runs the whole song: F# for 2 bars, G for 2 bars. Chorus is A for a bar, C and D sharing the next bar, then A for 2. Bridge is E for 2 bars then A for 2 bars, twice. 66 bars, about 2:31, and it is one unbroken crescendo from near silence to full strum.
songs.fallback: Barre F# at the 2nd fret and G at the 3rd, with open A, C, D and E for everything else. If the barres tire out, play F#5 and G5 on the bottom three strings and keep the pulse steady.
songs.rehearsalNotes: Campfire setlist extra. Skip for shows unless called. Solo piece: play the whole arrangement and sing it. Start almost silent so the crescendo has somewhere to go, and hard stop on the last A.

songs.title: Rusty Cage
songs.role: Solo arrangement: main riff and rhythm under your own vocal
songs.linkQuality: Songsterr song 39852 is a real 2009 human transcription of the Cash cut (aiGenerated false), acoustic guitar track, standard tuning, and it is what the Tabs sheet and this chart follow. Careful: the Chords tab on that same Songsterr page is a separate community submission that writes the song a minor third high (C, Am, G5), so ignore it. Ultimate Guitar 1883629 and guvnaguitars both agree with the tab at A5, G, E5. Do not use song 54221, which is Soundgarden's original with the low string dropped to B, or the AI regenerated Johnny Ca$h entry.
songs.scaleHint: Two halves a fourth apart, and both are a minor vamp with no third in the chord. The fast half sits on A5 with the low string walking E to G and back to A, so A minor pentatonic at the 5th covers all of it, and the G that ends each chorus phrase already lives in that box. When the song turns electric it drops to E5 for the rest of the track, so slide the same shape down to open position and use E minor pentatonic at frets 0 to 3, or move it to the 12th for the identical fingering. Aim at A in the fast half and E in the slow half. The D late in the coda is the same move as the G in the fast chorus, one whole step under the E5.
songs.mustKnow: One riff, moved once. Fast half at about 112: A5 held while the low string walks open E to the 3rd fret G and back, 8 bars an intro, 8 bars a verse, and a 4 bar chorus cell that pushes to G. About 1:26 in, the record turns electric and everything drops a fourth to E5 at roughly 97, and the D takes the G's job. 40 fast bars plus 34 slow bars lands at about 2:50, which matches the 2:49 album cut. Ends on a held chord, no fade.
songs.fallback: Skip the low walk and just strum A5 (x022xx) in the fast half and E5 (022xxx) in the slow half. The vocal carries the song either way. Open Em and a full G cover the ending if the power shapes feel thin, and a plain open Am works anywhere the A5 does.

songs.recordingNote: Johnny Cash, American II: Unchained (1996), Rick Rubin producing with Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers backing. Not a copy of Soundgarden's 1991 Badmotorfinger original. Chart the Cash cut only: Soundgarden drop the low string to B, Cash's band plays standard tuning in A, no capo. The record opens on driving acoustic and turns electric near the midpoint, about 1:26, where everything drops a fourth to E5. On tempo, the Songsterr transcription's own data carries exactly two tempo marks, 112 at bar 1 and 97 at bar 21, and that second one is worth trusting: at a flat 112 the whole form comes up about 10 seconds short of the 2:49 runtime, and Karaoke Version calls the track variable around 105, which is roughly the average of the two. Still a gear change in feel rather than a hard halftime. Bar counts inside each half are a best fit, not gospel, so check them against the record if a section feels off.

songs.title: Hi Ren
songs.role: Solo fingerstyle guitar under your own spoken and sung vocal
songs.linkQuality: Songsterr 673470 track 0 is a human editor transcription (aiGenerated false, moderator author), Drop D, and it covers the whole piece rather than one figure, so the in-app Tabs sheet is that import with the silent video tail trimmed. Careful with it: this repo's importer renders only the first voice, so the sustained bass note under the intro, the main line and the dyad groove is missing from the ASCII. The hand-written figures at the top of the Tabs sheet put it back. Ultimate Guitar 4989430 is the popular chords page and agrees on Dm, A, Bb and F. There is no rhythm-versus-lead choice to make here, since the record is one guitar.
songs.scaleHint: D minor is home, and the record leans on D harmonic minor because the A chord is a major five with a C# in it. Three of the four hook notes sit in the D minor pentatonic box: the line is F, C#, D and A on the G string at frets 10, 6, 7 and 2, and the C# is the odd one out, the raised seventh that belongs to the A chord. So play the box, and on the A bars raise the C to C# or just aim straight at the C#. The Gm in the spoken vamp brings a Bb, which is outside the box as well. Watch the box in Drop D, because the low string is a D, so the fret numbers on that one string sit two higher than a standard-tuning diagram shows. Open position works as well as the box, since the same five notes sit around the open Dm shape at frets 0 to 3.
songs.mustKnow: Dm A Bb F is the four-bar loop and it runs the whole piece, but it is not the only harmony: the spoken blocks drop to a two-bar Dm to Gm vamp, and the intro and the reset run Dm Gm Dm A. The loop turns up in three costumes. One is the picked intro melody in free time, marked 98 easing to 80. Two is a single pitch per bar on the G string at frets 10, 6, 7 and 2, around 110, struck on every beat with the roots underneath on the dropped low string. Three is the percussive Dm to Gm figure that trades with it all through the middle, open strings as the release. Then a chromatic climb in fifths on the low two strings, a slowed recap of the intro melody, and the last third is the loop again, picked at about 100 and then strummed as full barres with an F to Gm to Am climb closing every pass. Long-term project: the work is stamina, dynamics and the picking hand, not the chords.
songs.fallback: Strum the four chords. Dm, A, Bb, F, one bar each, all the way through. In Drop D you can also just play the roots on the low string at frets 0, 7, 8 and 3, which is exactly what the record does at the top of the last third. If the picked intro is not there yet, skip it and count yourself in on the loop. Standard tuning plays everything except those low D roots, so the tuning is a nice-to-have rather than a requirement.
songs.rehearsalNotes: Campfire setlist extra. Skip for shows unless called. Long-term technique project rather than a show song: nylon-string style fingerpicking under a spoken and sung piece that runs 8:35, so build it in chunks and do not try to run the whole thing early. Drop D. Natural end, hold the last chord.

songs.recordingNote: Ren's 2022 single, 8:35 on the streaming release, one nylon strung guitar and one voice with no band and no overdubs. Drop D, key of D minor. Tuning and key agree across the Songsterr transcription (song 673470, a human editor entry with aiGenerated false), GuitarTabsExplorer, and the published chord charts, which all list Dm, A, Bb, F and Gm. Shazam reports G minor at 103, which does not match the notes on the page, so ignore it. Tempo is not one number: the transcription carries marks at 98, 90, 80, 110 and 100, and the spoken passages are played in free time on top of that, so 110 is the main loop rather than the song's speed. Arithmetic warning, and it is a big one: the transcription's 162 sounding bars come to about 6:10 at its own tempo marks, against an 8:35 cut. The missing two and a half minutes is rubato, the free-time spoken stretches, and the long held ending, which the transcription writes out as 34 empty bars. Every cycle count on the cheat card is therefore approximate. Follow the vocal, not the bar count.

songs.title: The Tale of Jenny & Screech
songs.role: Solo fingerpicked guitar under your own sung and spoken storytelling
songs.linkQuality: Songsterr song 2221267 track 0 is a real human transcription (aiGenerated false, author RiceGamer064), standard tuning, one acoustic guitar, and it is the only entry that covers both tales end to end in a single file, so the in-app Tabs sheet is that import. Its 200 bars run about 7:20 at its own tempo marks, which is close enough to the released arc that the bar counts are usable, and nothing is hidden in a second voice, so the ASCII is complete. Careful with the other Ren entries on Songsterr: song 948881 is Jenny's Tale on its own and is human but written in Drop D, song 1718132 is Screech's Tale on its own on nylon strings, and song 1096837 is aiGenerated true, so ignore it. Ultimate Guitar has no page for the combined tale, only the two halves: 2620860 for Jenny's Tale and 2853143 for Screech's Tale. Between them they agree with the import at Am and Dm for the first half and Em, A, C and B for the second.
songs.scaleHint: Two tales, two keys, and that is the thing to hold in your head. Jenny's half is A minor and never leaves Am and Dm, so A minor pentatonic box 1 at the 5th covers all of it and the open Am shape covers the same notes down at the nut. Screech's half drops a fourth to E minor, which is the identical shape slid down to open position at frets 0 to 3, or moved up to the 12th if you want the fingering to match the diagram. Two notes sit outside the E minor box and both are worth aiming at on purpose. The A in Screech's chorus is a major chord, so it brings a C sharp: raise the C a semitone over that bar. The B is a major five, so it brings a D sharp: raise the D a semitone over that bar. The C in between is straight out of the key. Everything else in the second half is plain E minor pentatonic, and the low riff and the strummed ending both sit on the open strings.
songs.mustKnow: Two tales, two keys, one piece, about 7:20 of guitar. Jenny's half is a two bar fingerpicked loop, one bar of Am then one bar of Dm at about 85, and it runs from the end of the free time intro to the slowdown, roughly 19 passes. It gets loud once by moving the same two bars to Am and Dm barres at the 5th, then goes back to open shapes. Three chords turn the corner. Screech's half is E minor at about 130 and is built on a bass walk of E, F sharp, G and A under a picked melody, written in 3/4 the first time round and 4/4 when it drives. Its chorus is Em, A, C, B in 3/4 at about 110 and it comes round twice. The last third stays in that world: a low string riff, a picked Em to Bm pair, a minor line climb, then open Em to G to F sharp strummed hard. The ending walks C, Am, C, Em, A, C, B and holds. Natural end, no fade.
songs.fallback: Strum it. One bar of Am, one bar of Dm, all the way through Jenny's half, then Em, G and F sharp through Screech's with an A and a C where the chorus asks for them. If the free time intro is not there yet, start on the Am loop and let the voice count you in. Nothing needs a barre: the 5th fret Am and Dm in the middle are only there to get louder, and hitting the open shapes harder does the same job.
songs.rehearsalNotes: Campfire setlist extra. Skip for shows unless called. Solo piece: fingerpick it and tell the story. The chart is the combined tale, both halves back to back, so it is long and the work is stamina and the turn between them. The two halves are in different keys, A minor then E minor, and the amp goes one click up at the turn. Build it in chunks rather than running the whole thing early. Standard tuning. Natural end, hold the last chord. The story is a dark one, so know what you are singing before you play it for people.

songs.recordingNote: Ren's The Tale of Jenny and Screech, released 18 September 2019 on Freckled Angels. Chart the combined tale, not either half on its own. The material exists in two shapes: two separate official videos, Jenny's Tale and Screech's Tale, and the combined release, which on streaming is a five track run that plays straight through (Prologue 0:34, Jenny's Tale 3:08, Run Screech Run 0:12, Screech's Tale 3:27, Call for Backup 0:17, about 7:38 end to end) and on YouTube is one official music video. One nylon strung guitar and one voice, no band, standard tuning. Two keys, not one: Jenny's half is A minor on an Am to Dm loop and Screech's half is E minor. Tempo is not one number either. The Songsterr combined transcription (song 2221267, a human entry with aiGenerated false) marks free time for the picked intro, about 85 for Jenny's loop, 130 for Screech's half and 110 for its chorus, and it writes two stretches in 3/4 inside an otherwise 4/4 piece. Arithmetic check: its 200 bars come to about 7:20 at its own marks, against roughly 7:04 of released music once the spoken Prologue is taken off the front, so the extra is rubato and the held ending, and the counts on the cheat card are approximate. Follow the voice, not the bar count. One more trap: the standalone Jenny's Tale transcription (song 948881) is written in Drop D, which is a different arrangement of the same half, so do not mix it into this chart.

songs.title: Chalk Outlines
songs.role: Solo duet arrangement: fingerpicked loop under both sung parts
songs.linkQuality: Songsterr song 620375 track 0 is a real human transcription (aiGenerated false), standard tuning, no capo, one guitar, 71 written bars, and it covers the studio single end to end, so the in-app Tabs sheet is that import. Two things make it unusually trustworthy for this batch. Every measure carries exactly one voice, so this repo's first-voice-only importer loses nothing here, unlike the Hi Ren import. songs.recordingNote: Ren and Chinchilla, Chalk Outlines, released 15 December 2021 as a standalone single. It is not on Sick Boi, and the 2023 date some sources attach to it belongs to that album rather than to this track. Chart the studio single: 3:53, standard tuning, no capo, E major with the picked loop parked on its relative C sharp minor. A live outdoor duet video of the same song went up about ten days later on 25 December 2021 and runs near 4:28, so it is roughly half a minute longer and a good deal looser. The one available live transcription still centres on C sharp minor and E with no capo, so the key looks the same on both, but the length and the phrasing are not, and this chart follows the single. The seafront location usually given for that video, Brighton, could not be confirmed from any source, so do not repeat it as fact. Songsterr 620375 track 0 is the working source: a human transcription with aiGenerated false, one guitar, standard tuning, 71 written bars, and a single voice in every measure so nothing is hidden from this repo importer. Read it knowing that the strummed blocks are written in half time at 60 and 61 while the picked second verse is written at 122; the real grid is 122 all the way through, and a written bar in the half time blocks is two real bars. Arithmetic check: 118 real bars at 122 is 3:52 against the 3:53 release, so the cycle counts on the cheat card are solid rather than approximate, which is not true of the other Ren entries. One disagreement worth knowing: Ultimate Guitar 3990955 lists an F sharp minor to G sharp minor bridge in the last third. The guitar transcription has nothing of the kind there, only A, E, B and C sharp minor, so follow the tab.
